tip: To thank for something use за (za) plus the accusative: за обращение (za abrashchenie = for reaching out) after благодарим (blagadarim = we thank).
In a passive, the doer takes the instrumental: разработана инженерами (razrabotana = developed, inzhenerami = by engineers).
учась (uchas = while studying) comes from the reflexive учиться (uchitsya = to study) and keeps its reflexive -сь (-s) ending.
в течение (v techenie = within) takes the genitive: в течение трёх дней (tryokh dney = of three days).
Gerunds ending in -в mark an action finished before the main verb: подумав (padumav = having thought), then agreeing.
Short passive participles agree like adjectives: places are plural, so заняты (zanyaty = taken) takes the plural -ы ending.
In passives the doer goes in the instrumental case: учёным (uchyonym = by a scientist) after изобретено (izabreteno = invented).
полтора (paltara = one and a half) is followed by the genitive singular: полтора часа (paltara chasa = an hour and a half).
Gerunds ending in -я show action at the same time as the main verb: работая (rabotaya = working) while he saves time.
Collective numerals like двое (dvoe = two) count groups of people and take the genitive plural: двое детей (dvoe detey = two children).
After numbers грамм often keeps its short genitive plural: двести грамм (dvesti gramm = two hundred grams) in everyday speech.
Reflexive verbs ending in -ся build the gerund with -вшись: вернувшись (vernuvshis = having returned).
The position word до (do = until) takes the genitive: до встречи (do vstrechi = until the meeting), the usual way to say see you.
Adding -ся makes an ongoing passive with no named doer: обновляется (abnavlyaetsya = is being updated) needs no 'by whom'.
не за что (ne za shto = don't mention it) is the set reply to thanks, literally 'there is nothing to thank for'.
Good wishes drop 'I wish you' and put the noun in the genitive: хорошего вечера (kharoshevo vechera = good evening).
A plain they-form with no subject means 'will be done': построят (pastroyat = they will build) reads as a bridge will be built.
After a measure word the substance goes in the genitive: литр молока (litr malaka = a liter of milk), showing the amount.
оба (oba = both) takes the genitive singular noun, same as 2 to 4: оба брата (oba brata = both brothers), not the plural.
After 2, 3, 4 the noun is genitive singular: четыре месяца (chetyre mesyatsa = four months), never the plural form.
A few verbs form the -я gerund irregularly, giving лёжа (lyozha = lying) instead of the regular lezha form.
Future passive uses будут (budut = will be) plus a short participle: будут объявлены (budut abyavleny = will be announced).
Apologies use за (za = for) plus the accusative: извините за беспокойство (izvinite za bespakoystvo = sorry for the trouble).
In compound ordinals only the final word changes: двадцать первый (dvadtsat pervyy = twenty-first) puts the ending on the last part.
обе (obe = both) is the feminine form, matching сестры (syostry = sisters). Masculine or mixed groups take оба (oba).
Age uses the dative: ей (yey = to her), not она (ana = she). ей пятьдесят пять лет (yey pyatdesyat pyat let) means she is fifty-five.
семеро (semera = seven) is a collective numeral for a group of people, an everyday alternative to plain семь (sem).
две (dve = two) is the feminine form because капли (kapli = drops) is feminine. Masculine and neuter nouns take два (dva).
Work takes на (na), not в (v): на работе (na rabote = at work). Russian uses на for some locations where English says at or in.
построен (pastroyen = built) is a short passive participle and agrees with мост (most = bridge): masculine singular, so no ending.
